title: Exercise: Debounce a Bouncy Contact
oneLiner: Filter contact bounce out of a switch signal: only accept a change once the input has been steady for 50 ms, in both directions.
keyTakeaway: A TON resets whenever its input drops, so a TON on the signal and another on its inverse only finish when the signal has been steady for the whole time.
explanation:
Mechanical contacts bounce: when a switch closes, its contacts touch, spring apart and touch again several times before settling, and a fast input can see that as a burst of on/off changes. Debouncing means ignoring changes until the signal has been steady for a while.

Here the bounce is exaggerated to tens of milliseconds so that it shows up at a 10 ms scan; the same filter is used for chattering level switches and flickering photo-eyes.
